facts.content: An expansionary fiscal policy that does not change the interest rate has no effect on the exchange rate. Fiscal policy that raises output without affecting interest rates does not cause currency appreciation. In an open economy, a rise in output from expansionary fiscal policy can lead to currency appreciation only if it influences interest rates. When fiscal expansion leads investors to expect the central bank to raise interest rates, the currency tends to appreciate.

evidence.quote:
So an expansionary fiscal policy,
 which is accumulated by the Fed,
 that means the interest rate is kept at the same level,
 then does not lead to an appreciation of the currency.
It doesn't move the exchange rate.
It has no implication for the exchange rate.

It's because investors expect the Fed to react to that,
 or the central bank to react to that and raise interest rates.
